newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares close up, seen testing 1,140.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares close up, seen testing 1,140.

text.p: Austrian shares plodded higher on Tuesday, boosted by selective buying in cyclical shares, and some traders predicted the leading ATX index could hit 1,140 points by the end of the week.
"The market looks good at the moment and if the customers stay, it will climb higher," said one trader, noting 1,140 might be within reach this week.
But another said a bout of profit taking was more likely towards the end of the week after the Bundesbank meeting on Thursday. Most analysts do not expect the meeting to result in a rate cut.
"The markets are positive ahead of the Bundesbank meeting but we could see a setback after that," he said.
"It looks as though it will continue tomorrow with the highest volumes in cyclical shares and in those that are not so heavily weighted in the index," he added.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips edged up 2.85 points or 0.25 percent to 1,129.93. Among its constituents 11 ATX shares rose, eight fell and two remained unchanged.

Shares in steelmaker VA Stahl touch a record high at 393 schillings, but ease to close 5.20 schillings higher at 392.2 ahead of the company's nine-month results widely expected to be released on Monday.
The session's leading gainer was Austro Mikro Systeme, AMS, climbing 2.63 percent to 839.5 schillings.
Preferred shares of Creditanstalt were the top losers, falling 0.87 percent to 515 schillings.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index inched up 0.77 points or 0.18 percent to 427.33.
The December ATX future added 4.4 points to 1,128.8.
